issues.description: Inner contradiction in the problem statement about the type of the Animal.name attribute: the UML diagram (line 27) declares the attribute as type String, but the textual instructions in Part 1 (lines 84-86) explicitly require using StringBuilder for the name attribute. This conflicting specification can confuse students about which type to use when implementing Animal and its constructors/getters/setters.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the specification consistent: either update the UML in the problem statement to show name: StringBuilder, or change the textual instruction to require a String. Preferably update the UML to name: StringBuilder to match the explicit instruction, and clarify whether constructors should accept a String (and internally create a StringBuilder) or accept a StringBuilder directly.

issues.description: The reference solution's Animal implementation uses a String field for the name (private String name) whereas the problem text instructs students to use StringBuilder for the name attribute. This mismatch between the solution repository and the problem instructions may confuse students when they compare their implementation to the provided solution or to tests expecting a StringBuilder-based API/behavior.
issues.suggested_fix: Align the solution with the problem instructions: change the Animal.name field in the solution to a StringBuilder and update the constructor/getter/setter accordingly (or, if the intended design is to use String, update the problem statement to require String instead of StringBuilder). Also document whether constructors should accept String or StringBuilder to avoid further ambiguity.
